items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: if you go out to the west coast and hear the Turk Murphy offshoots... you have the California banjo-tuba-bass on Turk Murphy, and you have all these offshoots

ctx.x: When you were sitting by him in the polka bands, was it written music?

Yes, it was all written. A lot of triple time [scats]. Very similar really to two beat jazz. In fact it’s one of the things that I notice when I play in Germany. I think one of the reasons — my theory on one of the reasons that Germans love this red hot jazz, and they really love traditional jazz, it’s very similar to the polka. I mean [scats]. And if you go out to the west coast and hear the Turk Murphy offshoots, the 50 or so bands that are out there, it’s banjo and tuba, and it’s two-beat [scats]. And you can…
That’s a great point. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
